# Custom WGSL face shaders: contract and prelude

Generated from the engine's own catalogs, the same text Card Studio's describe-a-finish reads. Field lines read `` `key` (type or range): what it does ``; "— leave out" marks fields a design written from a description shouldn't set (uploads, licensed assets, internal state). A host that has its own images may still set them (`decals`, `surfaceSources`, `logo.src`). Section names in quotes ("Lighting", "Fonts") refer to headings in these references.

## Custom shaders

A layer `{ id: "custom", language: "wgsl", side, target, code }` runs your own WGSL fragment code on the card engine (WebGPU, or its WebGL 2 build). Always set `language: "wgsl"`: GLSL layers are skipped.

Rules:
- Define `fn mainImage(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f`: return display-sRGB colour and straight alpha (alpha 0 shows what's below). Don't write entry points (`@fragment`); don't redeclare any prelude name; helper `fn`s and `const`s are fine.
- It is WGSL, not GLSL: `vec2f` / `vec3f` / `vec4f`, `let` / `var`, `fn f(x: f32) -> f32`, no implicit int → float conversion (write `1.0`), `select(a, b, cond)` instead of `?:`, and `mod1` / `mod2` / `mod3` (prelude helpers) for GLSL's floored `mod` (WGSL's `%` truncates).
- `uv` is the face uv as you look at that face, (0,0) bottom-left. Prefer `facePos` (aspect-correct, centred, y in [-0.5, 0.5]) for patterns.
- Expose parameters as annotated module-scope declarations; the key in `params` is the declared name:
  - `var<private> uSpeed: f32; // @param 0 3 0.6 label="Speed"` (min max default; also `step=`, `description="…"`, `options="Soft:0,Hard:1"` for selects) on f32, i32, bool, vec2f, vec3f (`default=x,y` for vectors, `default=true` for bools)
  - `var<private> uTint: vec3f; // @color #f8cdda label="Tint"`
  - Unannotated declarations stay 0. Annotations are checked; mistakes come back as errors with line numbers.
- `// @replaces-artwork` anywhere hides the face's artwork (for shaders that redraw it via `artwork(uv)`).
- Using `uTime` or `uTilt` makes the layer animated; `uPointer` makes it react to the pointer.
- At most 20000 characters. Loops are capped at 10 000 iterations per pixel, but keep per-pixel work small (no huge loops or heavy ray marching): it runs on phones.
- Skin layers render into the face texture under the metal lighting, so a skin's colour still looks like metal (polish, clearcoat and holo apply on top). Overlays sit over the face; use them for view-dependent sheens (`viewDir`, `faceNormal`, `uEye`).
- Keep the chip area calm: blend with `smoothstep(0.0, 0.06, chipDistance(uv))`.

In scope (the prelude's declarations):
```wgsl
var<private> uTime: f32; // Seconds since the layer started (frozen layers: their Freeze time). Using it makes the layer animated.
var<private> uResolution: vec2f; // Face texture size in pixels.
var<private> uTilt: vec4f; // The card's tilt spring: xy position (card normal x/y), zw velocity. Using it makes the layer animated.
var<private> uPointer: vec3f; // Pointer on this face: xy = uv, z = 1 while over it.
var<private> uBaseColor: vec3f; // The card's base colour (display sRGB).
var<private> uHasArtwork: f32; // 1 when the face has artwork.
var<private> uChip: vec4f; // Chip bounds [cx, cy, hx, hy] in top-origin card uv. Prefer chipDistance(uv).
var<private> uAspect: f32; // Card width / height (3.37 / 2.125).
var<private> uSide: f32; // 0 on the front, 1 on the back.
var<private> uOverlay: f32; // 1 for overlay layers, 0 for skins.
var<private> uEye: vec3f; // Camera position in face space (overlays).
var<private> uOpacity: f32; // Layer opacity (the wrapper applies it for you).
var<private> cardUv: vec2f; // uv in front-card space: mirrored on the back so x runs the same way through the card.
var<private> facePos: vec2f; // Aspect-correct, centred: (uv − 0.5) · vec2f(uAspect, 1); y in [−0.5, 0.5].
var<private> viewDir: vec3f; // Unit vector to the eye, face space (+z out of the face). Overlays only; skins get (0,0,1).
var<private> faceNormal: vec3f; // (0, 0, 1) in face space.
var uArtwork: texture_2d<f32>; // this face's artwork (transparent when absent): use artwork(uv)
```

Helpers: `mod1(x: f32, y: f32) -> f32`, `mod2(x: vec2f, y: vec2f) -> vec2f`, `mod3(x: vec3f, y: vec3f) -> vec3f`, `hash12(p: vec2f) -> f32`, `hash22(p: vec2f) -> vec2f`, `noise(p: vec2f) -> f32`, `fbm(p: vec2f) -> f32`, `rot2(a: f32) -> mat2x2f`, `rotate(p: vec2f, a: f32) -> vec2f`, `palette(t: f32, a: vec3f, b: vec3f, c: vec3f, d: vec3f) -> vec3f`, `hsv2rgb(c: vec3f) -> vec3f`, `luma(c: vec3f) -> f32`, `srgbToLinear(c: vec3f) -> vec3f`, `linearToSrgb(c: vec3f) -> vec3f`, `sdRoundBox(p: vec2f, b: vec2f, r: f32) -> f32`, `chipDistance(uv: vec2f) -> f32`, `artwork(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f`, and `PI`, `TAU`.

Starter examples:

Plasma (skin): Animated cosine-palette plasma that keeps clear of the chip.
```wgsl
// Plasma: a starter skin shader. Edit me!
var<private> uSpeed: f32;   // @param 0 3 0.6 label="Speed"
var<private> uScale: f32;   // @param 1 12 4 label="Scale"
var<private> uTintA: vec3f; // @color #1d2b64 label="Shadow"
var<private> uTintB: vec3f; // @color #f8cdda label="Highlight"

fn mainImage(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
  let p = facePos * uScale;
  let t = uTime * uSpeed;
  let v = sin(p.x + t) + sin(p.y * 1.3 - t) + sin(length(p + vec2f(sin(t * 0.7), cos(t * 0.5))) * 1.7);
  var col = mix(uTintA, uTintB, 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(v * 1.6));
  // keep the area around the chip calm
  col = mix(uBaseColor, col, smoothstep(0.0, 0.06, chipDistance(uv)));
  return vec4f(col, 1.0);
}
```

Tilt spotlight (overlay): A soft light that slides across the face as the card tilts (overlay).
```wgsl
// A view-dependent glint: brightest where the reflected view meets a fixed light.
var<private> uColor: vec3f;    // @color #fff4d6 label="Light"
var<private> uSize: f32;       // @param 0.05 0.6 0.22 label="Size"
var<private> uStrength: f32;   // @param 0 1 0.55 label="Strength"

fn mainImage(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
  let r = reflect(-viewDir, faceNormal);
  let spot = r.xy * 1.8;                    // where the light lands on the face
  let d = length(facePos - spot * vec2f(uAspect, 1.0) * 0.5);
  let glow = exp(-d * d / (uSize * uSize)) * uStrength;
  return vec4f(uColor, glow);
}
```

Ripple rings (skin): Concentric rings from the pointer (or the centre), tinted by the artwork.
```wgsl
// Rings that follow the pointer while it is over the card.
// @replaces-artwork  (this shader redraws the artwork itself, so the card hides the original)
var<private> uRings: f32;    // @param 4 60 24 label="Rings"
var<private> uSpeed: f32;    // @param 0 4 1 label="Speed"
var<private> uUseArt: bool;  // @param default=true label="Tint with artwork"

fn mainImage(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f {
  let c = mix(vec2f(0.5), uPointer.xy, uPointer.z);
  let d = length((uv - c) * vec2f(uAspect, 1.0));
  let ring = 0.5 + 0.5 * cos(d * uRings * 6.2831 - uTime * uSpeed * 3.0);
  var base = uBaseColor;
  let art = artwork(uv);
  if (uUseArt && uHasArtwork > 0.5) { base = mix(base, art.rgb, art.a); }
  return vec4f(base * (0.75 + 0.35 * ring), 1.0);
}
```
